Release notes

Sourced from @​biomejs/biome's releases.

Biome CLI v2.5.14

2.5.14

Patch Changes

  • #9022 0d49e24 Thanks @​dyc3! - Added the nursery rule noReturnInFinally. This rule disallows return statements in Promise.prototype.finally() callbacks, including inside nested blocks and conditional branches. Returns in nested functions are ignored by the rule.

    // Invalid: return in finally callback
Promise.resolve(1).finally(() => { return 2 })

    // Valid: no return in finally callback
    
Promise.resolve(1).finally(() => { console.log(2) })

    Returning a value from a Promise.prototype.finally() callback does not replace the original promise's fulfillment value, which can be confusing. Returned promises and thenables are awaited, and their rejection rejects the resulting promise.

  • #11754 71eaa0d Thanks @​griff-rees! - Added the nursery rule noSvelteAtDebugTags, which disallows Svelte's {@debug} tag.

    <!-- Invalid: leftover debugging tag -->
{@debug user}

    The {@debug} tag is a debugging aid and should be removed once you no longer need it, as it should not remain in production code. The rule provides a safe fix that removes the tag.

  • #11725 5eb5f09 Thanks @​m1handr! - Added the nursery rule useValidTestTitle, which enforces valid titles for unit test cases and suites.

  • #11735 9bd70c7 Thanks @​ematipico! - Fixed #8471: source.fixAll.biome ignored formatter.formatWithErrors. It now applies safe fixes without formatting files that have parse errors when the option is disabled.

  • #11715 f05a3c3 Thanks @​ematipico! - Fixed #7771: Grit plugins that use sequential no longer panic when Biome processes files.

  • #11766 c2542c6 Thanks @​dyc3! - Fixed validation of readonly and accessor modifiers: combining them in either order now reports that they cannot be used together.

  • #11461 22e9966 Thanks @​FoundDream! - Fixed #11423: Multiline template interpolations now preserve the indentation of their closing brace when the source indentation is not a multiple of tabWidth.

  • #11766 c2542c6 Thanks @​dyc3! - Fixed #11763: TypeScript class members using override accessor, such as override accessor value = 1, now parse correctly. The reversed order, accessor override, now reports that override must precede accessor.

```
Seventeen visualization widgets built on one TypeScript core, wrapped for R
```

title: docs: stop counting components in the motivation
description:
Three sentences in `docs/motivation.md` said **seventeen**:

- "There are seventeen opinionated components, not composable primitives."
- "If your figure is not one of the seventeen here, plotly is the correct answer"
- "You need a figure that is not one of the seventeen."

The R package ships **fifteen**. The number was right for JavaScript and Python and wrong for an R reader, and it was the last place in the repository still saying seventeen flatly after #80 corrected the README and the landing page.

None of the three sentences needed it. Each argues that the set is fixed rather than composable, which does not depend on how many are in it. The component table on the landing page stays the one place the set is written down.

## Kept on purpose

> The claims above are architectural, not benchmarked. No formal performance comparison against these packages has been run, and this document does not assert specific frame rates.

That sits under the comparison table and is the honest thing to say there.

## Also

The `Architecture` link in the landing page list now says what is behind it. That document is written for someone working on the shared core, not someone using the package, and the bare link gave no hint.

title: docs: correct what the R package ships and give each page a licence
description:
## The claim that sent R users to the wrong place

`docs/index.html`, directly under the R install command:

> The CRAN release carries 15 of the 17 components; the genome-browser pair
> (igv.js and Gosling) ships in R from r-universe until a later release adds
> them to CRAN.

r-universe builds from `pkg-r/`, which has no igv or gosling source, no
`NAMESPACE` entry and no man page. The r-universe API returns 50 exports and
none of them match. An R user who follows that sentence installs from r-universe
and ends up with the same fifteen components.

The count itself was right. The sentence after it was not.

## Four places said four different things

| File | Said | True |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `README.md` | Seventeen components, each available in all three languages | R has fifteen |
| `pkg-r/README.md` | Fifteen, and a later release adds the other two back | Fifteen, and whether they return is #78 |
| `docs/index.html` meta | Seventeen widgets wrapped for R, including genome browsers | Fifteen |
| `docs/index.html` body | 15 of the 17 | Correct |

The component table now marks the two rows R does not have.

## Scale

Three files said millions of points stay interactive. `docs/motivation.md`
already answered that, in a section written to calibrate it: the largest figure
exercised in this repository is 500k. The prose now says several hundred
thousand.

## The registry pages

`pkg-py/README.md` and `pkg-js/README.md` had no licence line, and the npm page
linked no documentation anywhere. Both now point at the project overview.

The PyPI page never said it ships all seventeen components, which is the one
thing it has over the R package.

The PyPI page also carried `pnpm dist`, an editable install and `pytest`. That
belongs in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Examples

`examples/shiny-react-embedding/README.md` had a section headed "Using the local
(unpublished) plotomics build". The package has been on npm since 0.1.0 and is
at 0.2.0. Linking a local build is still worth documenting, so that stays
without the claim.

`examples/r-shiny/README.md` told readers to add a tab for `profile`, `igv` and
`gosling`. `profile` became `bioprofile` in 0.2.0, and neither browser is in the
R package.

## Quick start

The root README opened its R example with `devtools::load_all("pkg-r")` under a
heading reading "Quick start (dev)", above a `pnpm install`. plotomics is on
CRAN, so the example now starts at `library(plotomics)`. A JavaScript example
joins the R and Python ones, since the repository ships to npm.

Installation gained `npm install plotomics` for the same reason.

`examples/shiny-react-embedding/package.json` pins `plotomics: ^0.1.0`, which
cannot resolve to 0.2.0. That is a dependency change rather than a docs one.

title: docs: fix the badge rows and a broken install path
description:
## The install instruction was broken

`pkg-r/README.md` told the reader to run:

```r
pak::pak("samuelbharti/plotomics")
```

That fails. There is no `DESCRIPTION` at the repository root, because the package sits in `pkg-r/`. Same shape of bug as the one fixed in peacock.

```r
pak::pak("samuelbharti/plotomics/pkg-r")
```

## The downloads badge showed a meaningless number

```
https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/plotomics
```

cranlogs expects `/badges/<period>/<package>`. With the period missing, `plotomics` landed in the period slot. Using `grand-total` the badge now reads `CRAN downloads 119`. Closes #74.

## pkg-js had no badges

That file is the npm page, and npm is this package's primary registry. A reader arriving there saw no version, no licence and no DOI.

## Everything checked

```
CRAN status      CRAN 0.1.0
CRAN downloads   CRAN downloads 119
r-universe       r-universe: 0.2.0
npm              npm: v0.2.0
PyPI             pypi: v0.2.0
DOI              DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21926306
lifecycle        lifecycle: stable
```

The gap between CRAN 0.1.0 and the 0.2.0 elsewhere is real and unchanged by this. The badges report it rather than hiding it.

Licence badges linked to `opensource.org/licenses/MIT`, a path OSI retired, and now point at the repository `LICENSE`.

The headline read "with R and Python wrappers" while the same package ships on npm.

title: docs: serve the DOI badge from shields
description:
The DOI badge came from `zenodo.org`, whose badge endpoints are not dependable. Measured over five requests each:

```
zenodo.org/badge/DOI/<doi>.svg     timed out x5, 15 seconds each
zenodo.org/badge/<repo-id>.svg     403 x5
img.shields.io/badge/DOI-...       200 x5, 0.08 to 0.16 seconds
```

That is why a DOI badge often fails to appear on first load and then shows up on a refresh. The browser gives up waiting, and a later cached fetch succeeds.

The replacement is served by shields and renders `DOI: 10.5281/zenodo....`. The slash becomes `%2F`, and `1682D4` is Zenodo's blue, so it still reads as a DOI badge.

It is also static, which fixes a second problem. `zenodo.org/badge/<repo-id>.svg` resolves to whatever Zenodo currently thinks is newest, while the link stays pinned to whatever was written, so after a release the image and the link can name different DOIs. With the DOI in both halves they cannot disagree.

Every DOI in this change was checked and resolves.

title: ci: hold react and react-dom majors alongside pixi
description:
Follow-up to #62 and #65, both closed rather than merged, and to #69 which did the same for pixi.js.

All three are optional peer dependencies. Nothing in `pkg-js/src` imports any of them. They are declared because gosling.js and higlass need them, and those two hold every one below its current major:

```
gosling.js@1.0.7   pixi.js ^6.3.0
                   react, react-dom ^16.6.3 || ^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0
higlass@1.13.6     pixi.js ^5.0.3 || ^6.5.2
                   react, react-dom ^16.6.3 || ^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0
```

A major bump force-resolves both libraries against a version they do not support:

```
- gosling.js@1.0.7(pixi.js@6.5.10)(react-dom@18.3.1(react@18.3.1))(react@18.3.1)
+ gosling.js@1.0.7(pixi.js@6.5.10)(react-dom@18.3.1(react@19.3.0))(react@19.3.0)
```

pnpm permits this, because a peer mismatch is a warning rather than an error. CI then passes, because no test touches the components that use these libraries. Those are the genome browsers, Gosling and igv.js, which are also the two that ship from r-universe rather than CRAN.

There is a second problem specific to react. Dependabot proposes `react` and `react-dom` as separate pull requests, and they have to move together. Merging one alone leaves `react@19.3.0` with `react-dom@18.3.1`, which share no major and break at runtime on their own.

## Scope

Only majors are held, for these three names. Minor and patch updates arrive as usual, and the github-actions and pip ecosystems are untouched.

Upgrading gosling.js and higlass unblocks all three at once. Remove these entries at that point.

title: ci: add a workflow that rebuilds the committed bundles
description:
Every JavaScript dependency pull request in this repository is unmergeable as it arrives. Four had collected before this.

`pkg-r/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/plotomics` and `pkg-py/src/plotomics/static` hold built bundles, committed because the R and Python packages ship them. The js job in `ci.yml` rebuilds them and fails when the result differs:

```yaml
- name: Verify committed bundles are up to date
  run: |
    git add -A pkg-r/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/plotomics pkg-py/src/plotomics/static
    git diff --cached --exit-code ...
```

Dependabot updates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and never runs `pnpm dist`, so the bundles go stale and the check fails. Nothing dependabot can do fixes it.

## Why not rebuild them locally

The check compares byte for byte. A bundle built on a different operating system, Node version or toolchain can differ from what the runner produces, and committing one that CI then rejects blocks the branch for a different reason.

A rebuild attempt on Windows failed outright: pnpm placed every package in the store but created none of the nested dependency links, so esbuild could not resolve `graphology-utils` from `graphology-layout-forceatlas2`. The same branch builds cleanly on the ubuntu runner.

## What this does

`workflow_dispatch` only. It checks out the branch, runs the same steps as the js job on the same runner and Node version, and pushes the rebuilt bundles.

```bash
gh workflow run rebuild-bundles.yml --ref <branch>
```

The steps mirror `ci.yml` exactly, which is the point. Bundles verified in one environment have to be built in that environment.

## Safety

- Dispatch is the only trigger. Nothing automatic writes a commit.
- It refuses to run on the default branch, so it cannot push past the pull request rule.
- `git add` is scoped to the two bundle paths, so an unrelated build artifact cannot ride along.
- No force push.
- When the bundles already match, it reports that and commits nothing.

title: ci: stop dependabot proposing a pixi.js major
description:
Follow-up to #63, which was closed rather than merged.

pixi.js is an optional peer dependency. Nothing in `pkg-js/src` imports it. It is declared because two consumers need it, and both pin it to 6:

```
gosling.js@1.0.7  requires  pixi.js: ^6.3.0
higlass@1.13.6    requires  pixi.js: ^5.0.3 || ^6.5.2
```

A major bump resolves gosling against a pixi it does not support. pnpm permits this, because a peer mismatch is a warning rather than an error, so the lockfile ends up with `gosling.js@1.0.7(pixi.js@8.20.1)` and CI stays green.

CI stays green because no test exercises the components that use pixi. Those are the genome browsers, Gosling and igv.js, which are also the two that ship from r-universe rather than CRAN. A passing run says the parts that do not use pixi still work.

Without this, dependabot reopens the same pull request every week, and each one looks mergeable.

## Scope

Only the major is held. Minor and patch updates to pixi.js still arrive as usual, and the other two ecosystems are untouched.

Moving pixi means upgrading gosling and higlass first. When that happens, remove this entry.

title: ci: check correctness before bundle drift
description:
The JS job ran in this order:

```
pnpm lint
pnpm dist
Verify committed bundles are up to date
typecheck
test
```

The bundle check compares a fresh build against the committed bundles in `pkg-r/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/plotomics` and `pkg-py/src/plotomics/static`. Any dependency bump changes the build output, so the check fails and the job stops there. `typecheck` and `test` never run.

That is why all four open dependency pull requests fail at the same step, and why none of them carries any evidence about the code itself:

```
#61  bump the npm-minor-patch group     Verify committed bundles are up to date
#62  bump react-dom 18.3.1 -> 19.3.0    Verify committed bundles are up to date
#63  bump pixi.js 6.5.10 -> 8.20.1      Verify committed bundles are up to date
#65  bump react 18.3.1 -> 19.3.0        Verify committed bundles are up to date
```

`#63` is the one that matters. pixi.js drives the rendering, and a two-major jump is exactly the change that needs typecheck and tests to report. At the moment it is impossible to tell whether that version works at all, because a stale bundle stops the job first.

Bundle drift on a dependency bump is expected and mechanical. It is not the interesting failure, and it should not hide the interesting one.

## Change

`typecheck` and `test` now run before the bundle check. Nothing is removed or weakened: the bundle check still runs on every pull request, still stages with `git add -A` so a missing bundle fails too, and still fails a stale one.

title: fix: resolve the PEP 639 license conflict in the Python package
description:
`pkg-py/pyproject.toml` declared the licence twice:

```toml
license = "MIT"                                    # SPDX expression, PEP 639
classifiers = [
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",      # the old way
]
```

PEP 639 makes those mutually exclusive. setuptools already errors on the combination and hatchling is moving the same way. The `[build-system]` block asked for `hatchling` with no lower bound, so a future hatchling release could break the build without any change in this repository.

The wheel also shipped no licence text. `pkg-py/` had no `LICENSE` file and nothing declared one.

## Changes

1. Pin `hatchling>=1.27`, the first release that understands the PEP 639 fields.
2. Drop the `License ::` classifier and add `license-files = ["LICENSE"]`.
3. Add `pkg-py/LICENSE`, copied from the repository root.
4. Add the `Typing :: Typed` classifier. The `py.typed` marker already ships, so the marker worked while the discoverability did not.
5. Add `Source` and `Changelog` to `[project.urls]`. `Source` points at `tree/main/pkg-py`, so PyPI links to the package rather than the repository root.

## Verified

`uv build` succeeds and the wheel metadata now reads:

```
Metadata-Version: 2.5
License-Expression: MIT
License-File: LICENSE
```

with `plotomics-0.2.0.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE` present and no `License ::` classifier.

title: fix: publish to npm with trusted publishing instead of a token
description:
The npm job carried a long-lived `NPM_TOKEN` and also requested an OIDC token for provenance. That combination signs the provenance but still authenticates with the token, so it is not trusted publishing. A publish-scoped credential sat in the repository secrets for no benefit.

This removes the `env:` block. Authentication becomes OIDC.

## Before merging

Connect the npm Trusted Publisher at https://www.npmjs.com/package/plotomics/access. It must name this repository and the workflow file `release.yml`, and leave the environment empty, because the npm job declares no environment.

After the publisher is connected, delete the `NPM_TOKEN` secret from the repository settings.

## On pnpm

The job publishes with `pnpm publish`, not `npm publish`. pnpm 11.0.8 broke the OIDC exchange and returned 404 (pnpm/pnpm#11513). The fix landed in May 2026 and this repository pins pnpm 11.9.0, so it carries the fix. The workflow comment records this, so a 404 at the publish step points at the right cause instead of looking like a misconfigured publisher.

Nothing breaks before the next tagged release. The publish step runs only on a `v*` tag.

title: chore: acknowledge advisors and funders across the packages

Adds the same author and acknowledgement metadata that biobouncer carries:
two thesis advisors, and Posit Software, PBC as a funder and copyright
holder.

  funder (`cph`, `fnd`). Samuel Bharti also gains the `cph` role, to match

  page sidebar (`roles: [aut, cre, ths, fnd]`). The footer keeps the

  section.
* `pkg-r/man/plotomics-package.Rd` is regenerated by roxygen2.

Python docs are built with pdoc, and JS has no doc generator, so there is no
equivalent footer setting to add there; the README sections cover both.

`CITATION.cff` is left as is, matching the choice made in biobouncer to keep
citation authorship to the maintainer.

## Checks

* `roxygen2::roxygenise("pkg-r")` regenerates cleanly.
* This repo has no pre-commit config; the diff is README prose and R
  metadata only, nothing that touches the JS/Python build or lint.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.1 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

title: feat(brand): add the hex logo and favicon
description:
## Summary

Adds the project hex sticker, a favicon, and the script that builds both.

The mark is a tissue section split down the middle: binned into solid hexagonal cells on the left, drawn point by point on the right. Both halves are sampled from the same density field, so the two sides always describe the same data. The contrast between them is the argument for the library, which is why the logo makes it rather than showing a chart.

Drawn on the real R hexSticker geometry (pointy-top, 2 by 2.31 inches) so it translates directly to a printed sticker.

## What is included

| File | Size | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `assets/logo.svg` | vector | source of truth |
| `assets/logo.png` | 1200x1379 | print resolution, transparent ground |
| `pkg-r/man/figures/logo.svg` / `.png` | 240x276 | R convention, pkgdown picks it up automatically |
| `assets/favicon.svg` / `.png` | 512x512 | reduced mark |
| `docs/favicon.svg` | vector | replaces the placeholder blue data URI on the docs site |

The favicon is a reduction rather than a shrink. At 16px the lattice and the three tissue layers both stop registering, so neither is drawn and only the split survives.

## Palette

Deliberately avoids the Flat UI set that `BiocStickers` recommends, and Bioconductor blue, since that is why so many bioinformatics stickers look interchangeable. Also inverts the usual value structure: a pale ground rather than a dark one, so it separates from the other stickers on a laptop lid.

- `#EDE6D8` bone ground
- `#8E2A3C` oxblood
- `#C4643F` clay
- `#3A3634` graphite

## Notes

- `scripts/make-logo.mjs` is seeded, so `pnpm logo` reproduces every committed file byte for byte. Verified across repeated runs, including after reformatting.
- One new devDependency, `@resvg/resvg-js`, does the SVG to PNG step.
- Point placement is controlled by a single `SEED` constant; changing it reshuffles the scatter and nothing else.

title: feat(violin): add the stacked violin component
description:
Stacks on #33. Base is `feat/upset-component`; retarget once that lands.

One row per feature, one violin per group. A box plot hides bimodality, which
in single-cell data is usually the whole story: a gene expressed in half a
cluster and silent in the other half has the same median as one expressed
weakly everywhere.

The component draws densities, it does not estimate them. Each violin arrives
as a vector on a shared grid, because kernel bandwidth choice changes what the
figure claims and belongs with the data rather than the renderer. It also keeps
the payload proportional to the grid instead of the cell count, which is what
makes a marker panel over thousands of cells cheap to ship.

`violin_density()` does the estimation in R, evaluating every group on one grid
spanning all of them. Groups too small to estimate return a flat row rather
than an error, since a cluster with one cell is a real thing to encounter.

## Per-feature grids

The second commit adds an optional `meta.grids`, one grid row per feature. This
was not speculative: on real Visium data a single shared grid meant one gene
reaching 7.4 compressed every other row into a flat line, and the rows that
vanished were the ones worth looking at. Clusters still share a scale within a
feature, which is the comparison a marker panel is read for.

`gridForRow()` falls back to the shared grid when `grids` is absent or too
short, so a partial feed loses the per-row scaling rather than blanking a row.

## Checks

- 172 JS tests (up from 159), 423 R tests (up from 382)
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `ruff` clean, `pnpm dist` rebuilds 17 anywidget and 17
  umd bundles
- Full recipe: entries, subpath export, unit tests, `dev/main.ts` demo with a
  deliberately bimodal feature, R wrapper with htmlwidgets assets and testthat
  coverage, Python wrapper

One test caught a real polygon indexing mistake in my own assertion rather than
the code, and the symmetry test now pins the mirrored half explicitly.

title: feat(upset): add the set-intersection component
description:
Stacks on #32. Base is `feat/km-component`, so this PR's diff is just the new
component; retarget once #32 lands.

Venn diagrams stop being readable at four sets and stop being drawable at five.
UpSet replaces the areas with an explicit matrix: a column per intersection, a
filled dot in every set it belongs to, a bar above for its size. It scales to
dozens of sets and stays exact.

Intersections are **exclusive**: a column counts the elements in precisely that
combination and no others. That is what makes the columns sum to the union
rather than double-counting, and it is why a small `A + B` bar next to large `A`
and `B` bars is evidence of mutual exclusivity rather than an artefact of the
chart.

`upset_intersections()` computes them from a logical matrix, along with per-set
totals and the universe size. Its test asserts the invariant that matters:
summing an element's exclusive intersections back up per set has to return that
set's total, which catches any off-by-one in the bitmask encoding.

Column order is the caller's, since which intersections are worth showing is an
analysis decision.

## Checks

- 159 JS tests (up from 150), 382 R tests (up from 353)
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `ruff` clean, `pnpm dist` rebuilds 16 anywidget and 16
  umd bundles

title: Gene treemap (D3 hierarchy + canvas)
description:
## Component

`treemap` — hierarchical gene-set / pathway composition. A flat edge list is
stratified into a hierarchy and laid out as a treemap; tiles render on a
**canvas** (fast at thousands of leaves — never one DOM node per tile) while an
**SVG overlay** carries only the low-cardinality vector layer: labels for tiles
above a minimum side, a drill-down **breadcrumb**, and a pointer tooltip. Click
a tile to zoom into that node; click a breadcrumb crumb to zoom back out.

Mirrors the Volcano reference: exported pure helpers (`buildRows`,
`buildHierarchy`, `topAncestorId`, `tileFitsLabel`, `valueExtent`) + a
`BiovizFactory` returning a `BiovizInstance`, with `exportSVG` (hybrid
rasterized tiles + vector overlay) and `exportPNG`.

## Library + version

- **d3-hierarchy `^3.1.2`** (latest; `stratify` + `treemap` + `treemapSquarify`
  / `treemapBinary`), with `@types/d3-hierarchy ^3.1.7`.
- Colors via `@bioviz/core`: `categoricalScale` (Okabe-Ito) for `colorBy:
  "parent"`, `ramp` (viridis / rdbu) for `colorBy: "value"`.

## Data contract

Flat tree as columns `{ id: string[], parent: string[], value: number[] }`
(root has empty / `NA` parent) plus `meta.labels?: string[]`. Built with
`d3.stratify`; internal-node values are summed from leaves. String columns
(`id`, `parent`) travel as JSON; the numeric `value` column uses the binary
transport (`pack_columns`) on the Python path.

## Options (camelCase, identical across JS / R / Python)

| Option | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `tile` | `"squarify"` \| `"binary"` | `"squarify"` |
| `paddingInner` | px | `1` |
| `colorBy` | `"parent"` \| `"value"` | `"parent"` |
| `colormap` | `"viridis"` \| `"rdbu"` | `"viridis"` |
| `labelMinSize` | px min tile side to draw a label | `32` |

## Performance

Tiles are rasterized in a single canvas pass (one `fillRect` per leaf); only
tiles wider/taller than `labelMinSize` get an SVG `<text>` label, so the vector
overlay stays low-cardinality regardless of leaf count. Dev demo mounts a
synthetic 12-pathway / ~5k-leaf hierarchy (`pnpm --filter @bioviz/components dev`).

## Verification (all pass from repo root)

- `pnpm install && pnpm dist` — builds `treemap` anywidget (16.7 kb) + umd
  (15.6 kb) bundles, synced into R and Python.
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" test` — 13 passed (9 new treemap helpers).
- `roxygen2::roxygenise("r/bioviz")` — regenerated `NAMESPACE` + `man/*.Rd`.
- `devtools::test("r/bioviz")` — 28 passed, 0 failures.
- `pytest -q` (python) — 9 passed (incl. pandas DataFrame path).

## Files

New: JS factory + entries + test, R `treemap.R` + binding/yaml + test +
generated `man/treemap*.Rd`, Python `treemap.py` + test. Appended (sorted only):
`lib/index.ts`, `dev/main.ts`, `python/src/bioviz/__init__.py`. No changes to
`@bioviz/core` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `allowBuilds`.

## Caveats

- Drill-down re-lays out a **copy** of the focus subtree to fill the plot area;
  color-by-value normalizes to the extent of the *currently visible* leaves, so
  the value ramp is relative to the zoom level.
- Malformed hierarchies (no root / multiple roots / cycle) render empty rather
  than throwing across the host boundary.
- Not merged.

title: feat: Python tests for the eight uncovered wrappers
description:
The R package has testthat coverage for all 17 components. The Python package had tests for 9. This closes that gap for the other eight: `dotplot`, `km`, `lollipop`, `oncoplot`, `profile`, `spatial`, `upset` and `violin`.

## It found a real bug

`Oncoplot` was broken and shipped that way. Every construction raised:

```
ValueError: columns must all have the same length; got codes=9, tmb=3, freq=3
```

The grid is `nrows * ncols`, the burden is one per sample and the frequency is one per gene, so the three columns are deliberately different lengths. `pack_columns` defaults to requiring equal lengths, and the call did not opt out. `network` is the only other wrapper that packs mixed lengths and it passes `equal_length=False`; `oncoplot` just missed it.

The R wrapper was never affected, since `plotomics_widget` has no equal-length check.

## What the tests assert

Ported from the invariants the R suite already encodes:

- **Row-major flattening**, for `violin` density, `upset` membership, `km` risk counts and the `oncoplot` grid. This is the failure mode that looks plausible on screen and is wrong, so each test checks a violin or intersection reads back its own row rather than a blend of its neighbours.
- **Order taken from a pandas Categorical**, for `violin`, `km` and `dotplot`. A dot plot's diagonal only appears under a stated order.
- **Input validation**, one test per wrapper covering the guards on shape, range and unknown categories.
- **`memo_sort`** for `oncoplot`, including that it produces the staircase rather than just sorting by frequency.
- **`lollipop` label resolution**, which happens server-side so a redraw, an export and any static counterpart label the same stems.

## Verification

171 passed, 0 skipped, up from 96 passed with 3 skipped.

Two caveats worth knowing:

- The three `Categorical` tests use `pytest.importorskip("pandas")`, and pandas is not in the `dev` extra, so **they will skip on CI**. I installed it locally to confirm they actually pass. Adding pandas to `dev` would be a reasonable follow-up.
- CI is currently billing-blocked on this repo, so every job fails in about two seconds without running a step. Everything above was run locally.

`ruff check` passes on all new files. The repo is not ruff-formatted overall and CI does not run ruff, so no unrelated files were reformatted here.

title: feat: add oncoplot, lollipop, profile and spatial components
description:
Third of three stacked PRs. Merge #29 and #30 first; until then this PR's diff
shows their commits too.

Four new components, taking the set from nine to thirteen, plus one change to
`embedding`. All four were driven by real pages in the omics gallery
(samuelbharti/omics-visualization-gallery#3) rather than designed in the
abstract, so each one has a caller proving the API works.

## Components

**`oncoplot`** - the gene x sample alteration grid every cancer-genomics paper
opens with, plus per-sample burden above, per-gene frequency to the right, and
clinical annotation strips below. 25 x 967 is over 24,000 cells, so the grid,
both marginal barplots and the strips all draw on one canvas, with labels and
the legend as an SVG overlay.

**`lollipop`** - mutation stems along a protein over its Pfam domain
architecture, with a PTM track underneath. Built on a track model so it can
carry peptide coverage later without a new component.

**`profile`** - grouped categorical bars with a block banner. Written for SBS96
mutational signatures, where the 96 trinucleotide contexts sit under six
substitution blocks, but it is general enough to serve a TMB waterfall or a
binned genomic profile.

**`spatial`** - an image underlay with a canvas point layer, for a tissue map.
The image and the points share one contain-fit transform computed once, so
histology and overlay cannot drift apart on resize or full-screen. Takes both
categorical and continuous point colouring, and is shaped to accept per-point
proportion vectors later for a deconvolution scatterpie.

## The embedding change

Categorical colouring assigned palette entries in first-appearance order, so
which colour a category got depended on which row happened to come first.
Shuffle the rows and the legend changes underneath you.

disagreed about what a colour meant.

## Summary

Two small, additive enhancements used by the omics-visualization-gallery app:

- **core:** add `ltc` (sequential) and `ltcdiv` (diverging) colour ramps derived
  from the LTC colour palettes, alongside the existing `viridis` / `rdbu`. Both

- **embedding:** add a `padding` option (default `0.04`) that controls how much
  the fitted view is padded around the data extent, so callers can zoom the
  camera out a little.

The gallery app uses `ltc` / `ltcdiv` to make the WebGL heatmaps match the
ggplot2 colour scheme, and the embedding `padding` to give the single-cell UMAP
some breathing room.

title: feat: add the km and dotplot components
description:
Stacks on #31. Base is `feat/omics-gallery-components`, so this PR's diff is
just the two new components; retarget to `main` once #31 lands.

Two components driven by real pages in the omics gallery
(samuelbharti/omics-visualization-gallery#4), taking the set from 13 to 15.

## `km` - Kaplan-Meier survival

A right-continuous step curve per stratum, censoring ticks, a pointwise
confidence band, and the number-at-risk table underneath. The table is on by
default because a survival curve without one hides how much of its tail rests
on a handful of patients, which is exactly where readers over-read it.

The component draws, it does not estimate. Everything arrives computed, so a
host that renders the same figure server-side can hand both renderers one set
of numbers and they cannot disagree about where a curve steps.

The R wrapper takes a `survfit` object directly, reading curves, censoring
times and at-risk counts off it. It prepends the `(0, 1)` origin per stratum,
which `survfit` does not store and without which every curve starts partway
down its first drop.

## `dotplot` - marker gene dot plot

Features down the rows, groups across the columns, dot size as the share
expressing and colour as the level. Two channels because colour alone cannot
separate "high in a few cells" from "moderate in all of them", and that
distinction is usually what decides whether a gene is a marker.

Dot **area**, not radius, is proportional to the percentage. A linear radius
quadruples the ink for a doubled percentage, which is the standard way a dot
plot overstates its strongest cells. The size legend reuses the same
`dotRadius` helper, so the swatches are literally the scale the dots use.

Row and column order is the caller's: sorting genes by the group they best mark
is an analysis decision. A factor supplies it in R, a pandas Categorical in
Python.

title: Genome viewer (igv.js)
description:
## Genome viewer (igv.js)

Adds the **`igv`** component: an embeddable interactive genome browser backed by [igv.js](https://github.com/igvteam/igv.js).

**Library:** `igv` **3.8.3** (added via `pnpm --filter @bioviz/components add igv`; no new `allowBuilds:` entry required). The bundle is ~1.5 MB — expected and acceptable for a full genome browser.

### Config contract (config-driven, not columnar)
igv.js streams and tiles remote indexed files (BAM/CRAM, bigWig, VCF, BED, ...) itself, so there is **no binary transport** — data flows entirely through the browser config as URLs. The `data` channel is unused (`setData` is a no-op).

Options (camelCase keys, identical across JS / R / Python):

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `config` | A full igv.js browser config (`{ genome\|reference, locus, tracks: [...] }`). When present it is passed through as-is and the convenience fields are ignored. |
| `genome` | Genome id (default `"hg38"`), used when `config` is absent. |
| `locus` | Initial locus string / gene symbol. |
| `tracks` | Array of igv.js track configs, used when `config` is absent. |

The pure `assembleConfig(options)` helper builds the config from convenience fields (or passes `config` through), omitting empty values so igv.js applies its own defaults. It lives in `igv-config.ts` (free of the igv import) so it is unit-testable headless.

### Async lifecycle
- `createIgv(el, {options})` returns a `BiovizInstance` **synchronously**, then kicks off `igv.createBrowser(el, config)` (which returns `Promise<Browser>`) asynchronously.
- `setOptions` with a new `locus` calls `browser.search(locus)`; a locus requested before the browser resolves is **buffered** and replayed once the promise settles. New entries in `tracks` are additively loaded via `browser.loadTrack`.
- `resize()` nudges igv.js via `igv.visibilityChange()` (igv tracks its own container size); it is a no-op until the browser is ready.
- `exportSVG()` returns `browser.toSVG()` once live, else `null`.
- `destroy()` calls `igv.removeBrowser(browser)` and clears the element; a `destroyed` guard tears down a browser whose `createBrowser` promise resolves after destroy (no leak).

Note: `igv`'s `main` field is a UMD bundle without a `default` export, so the runtime value is imported from `igv/dist/igv.esm.js` (with a local `igv-esm.d.ts` remapping types to the package root); esbuild then bundles a proper default export.

### Wrappers
- **R:** `igv(genome = "hg38", locus = NULL, tracks = list(), config = NULL, ...)` + Shiny bindings `igvOutput()` / `renderIgv()`. Config is assembled into the options list.
- **Python:** `IGV(genome="hg38", locus=None, tracks=None, config=None, ...)`.
- **Dev demo:** `dev/main.ts` `igv` entry — hg38 at `chr8:127,736,588-127,739,371` with a public ENCODE bigWig track.

### Shared-file edits (appended, sorted)
`packages/components/src/lib/index.ts`, `packages/components/dev/main.ts`, `python/src/bioviz/__init__.py`. Everything else is new files. Generated `man/igv.Rd`, `man/igv-shiny.Rd` and `NAMESPACE` are committed.

### Verification (all pass)
- `pnpm install && pnpm dist` — builds + syncs (igv umd/anywidget bundles ~1.5 MB).
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" test` — 9 passed (5 igv `assembleConfig` cases + 4 volcano).
- `roxygen2::roxygenise("r/bioviz")` + `devtools::test("r/bioviz")` — PASS 22.
- `pytest -q` (python `.venv`) — 9 passed (4 new igv).

title: feat(embedding): add equal-aspect and point scale mode options
description:
Adds two embedding options, both backward-compatible (defaults preserve current behaviour).

- pointScaleMode (asinh default, plus linear and constant): constant sizes points in literal pixels regardless of zoom, so a small or widely-scaled scatter (PCA scores, tissue coordinates) stays visible instead of flooring at one pixel.
- aspect (fill default, plus equal): equal gives both axes the same units per pixel for scores where relative spread matters.
- setOptions now honours pointSize and opacity (previously only applied at construction).

Python and R wrappers, tests, and committed bundles updated.

🚨 Behavior Change

    • Container.updateTransform({ scaleX: 0, scaleY: 0 }) previously coerced a zero scale to 1 (the code used opts.scaleX || 1), so passing 0 left the container at full size. It now applies zero scale literally, matching scale.set(0, 0). If you relied on updateTransform ignoring a zero scale, stop passing 0 when you mean full scale.
    const container = new Container();
container.updateTransform({ scaleX: 0, scaleY: 0 });
// before: scale coerced to (1, 1) — container stayed full-size
// after:  scale applied as (0, 0) — container hidden, matching scale.set(0, 0)
  • fix: particle container inherit blend mode by @​DmitriyGolub in pixijs/pixijs#11978
    • ParticleContainer now respects the blend mode inherited from its ancestors. Previously the render pipe read the container's own local blendMode instead of the resolved groupBlendMode, so setting e.g. stage.blendMode = 'add' had no effect on particles. Particles nested under a parent with a non-default blend mode will now render differently (e.g. additive brightening) where they were silently ignored before. Updates `esbuild` from 0.24.2 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

title: build(deps-dev): bump the npm-minor-patch group across 1 directory with 2 updates
description:
Bumps the npm-minor-patch group with 2 updates in the / directory: [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild) and [igv](https://github.com/igvteam/igv.js). Updates `esbuild` from 0.24.2 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

title: Network graph (Sigma v3 + graphology)
description:
## Component

`network` — a WebGL node-link diagram for large gene/protein interaction networks. Renders with **sigma v3** over a **graphology** graph model so tens of thousands of nodes/edges stay interactive. Follows the volcano reference structure: pure helpers + a `BiovizFactory` returning a `BiovizInstance`, exposed through anywidget (Python) and htmlwidgets (R) adapters.

## Libraries + versions

| Library | Version | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `sigma` | `^3.0.3` | WebGL renderer (multi-canvas: edges/nodes/labels/hovers/mouse) |
| `graphology` | `^0.26.0` | Graph data model |
| `graphology-layout-forceatlas2` | `^0.10.1` | Force-directed layout when coords are absent |

Added via `pnpm --filter @bioviz/components add`. `graphology-types` (peer) resolved automatically. No `allowBuilds:` entry was required (only `esbuild` is listed, already `true`).

## Data contract

Nodes and edges arrive as one `BiovizData`. Numeric columns go through the packed binary buffer (Python) or JSON arrays (R); strings/metadata via `data.columns` / `data.meta`.

- `columns.id` `string[]` — node ids (required)
- `columns.x`, `columns.y` `number[]` — optional precomputed coordinates
- `columns.size` `number[]` — optional per-node radius (px)
- `columns.source`, `columns.target` `string[]` — edge endpoints (index-aligned)
- `columns.weight` `number[]` — optional per-edge weight
- `meta.nodeLabels` `string[]` — optional labels (default: id)
- `meta.nodeGroup` `string[]` — optional categorical group → palette color
- `meta.edges` `[src,tgt][]` — alternative edge form (pairs of ids)

Edges referencing unknown nodes, self-loops, and parallel edges are dropped (undirected simple graph).

## Layout approach

`layout: "forceatlas2"` runs `forceAtlas2.assign(graph, { iterations, settings: inferSettings(graph) })` **only** when both x/y columns are absent; iterations are clamped to `[1, 2000]`. Nodes without coordinates are seeded on a unit ring so ForceAtlas2 has a non-degenerate start. `layout: "precomputed"` uses the supplied x/y and never runs a layout.

## Options (camelCase, identical across JS/R/Python)

`layout`, `iterations`, `defaultNodeColor`, `defaultEdgeColor`, `labelThreshold`, `defaultNodeSize`, `palette` (optional override; else `@bioviz/core` Okabe-Ito palette).

## Interactions

Hovering a node highlights it and its `graph.neighbors`, dims the rest via sigma `nodeReducer`/`edgeReducer`, and shows a tooltip (label, group, degree). Zoom/pan use sigma's built-in camera.

## Export

Sigma is WebGL, so there is no true vector output; `exportPNG(scale)` and `exportSVG()` composite sigma's canvas layers (`getCanvases()`) over the theme background into a single raster (SVG wraps it as an `<image>`).

## Files

- **JS**: `components/network.ts` (factory + sigma), `components/network-core.ts` (pure, GPU-free helpers — split out because sigma touches WebGL globals at import time, which breaks the Node test env), `entries/{anywidget,umd}/network.ts`, `test/network.test.ts`. Appended to `lib/index.ts` and `dev/main.ts` (synthetic 5k-node, 8-community clustered graph).
- **R**: `R/network.R` (`network(nodes, edges)` + `networkOutput`/`renderNetwork` Shiny bindings), `inst/htmlwidgets/network.{js,yaml}`, `tests/testthat/test-network.R`, generated `man/network*.Rd` + `NAMESPACE`.
- **Python**: `network.py` (`Network(nodes, edges)`, DataFrames or dicts), appended to `__init__.py`, `tests/test_network.py`.

## Verification (all pass from repo root)

- `pnpm install && pnpm dist` — builds `network.js` (anywidget 173 KB, umd 172 KB), synced to R + Python.
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" test` — 14 passed (10 network + 4 volcano).
- `roxygen2::roxygenise("r/bioviz")` — clean (second pass, no warnings).
- `devtools::test("r/bioviz")` — 32 passed.
- `pytest -q` (python venv, `pip install -e ".[dev]"`) — 11 passed.

## Caveats

- No true vector export (WebGL); PNG/SVG are composited rasters.
- The factory (sigma) is exercised only in the browser/dev harness; the Node test suite covers the pure helpers (graph build, edge parsing, group color, layout guard) — matching the "pure logic unit-tested without a GPU" architecture rule.
- Very large graphs (100k+ nodes) render well, but ForceAtlas2 layout time grows with node/edge count; the dev demo uses 5k nodes to keep in-browser layout snappy. Supply precomputed x/y for the largest graphs.

Do not merge.

title: Clustered heatmap + dendrograms
description:
## Component: `clustermap`

A hierarchically-clustered expression heatmap with dendrograms (in the spirit of `seaborn.clustermap` / Morpheus). Center is the heatmap, top is the column dendrogram, left is the row dendrogram, plus a colorbar legend below.

**Rendering split (per repo rules):** the data layer (every cell) is drawn on a **canvas** — one `ImageData` pixel per cell in a small offscreen buffer, GPU nearest-neighbour upscaled to the display canvas — so large matrices stay smooth and never touch per-cell DOM. Dendrograms, tick labels, colorbar and frame are a **crisp SVG overlay**. `exportSVG()` composites the rasterized heatmap (`<image>`) under the vector overlay; `exportPNG(scale)` flattens the offscreen cells + rasterized overlay into one high-DPI canvas.

## Library + version

- **`ml-hclust@4.0.0`** (mljs) — agglomerative nesting via `agnes(data, { method, distanceFunction })`, returning a `Cluster` tree (`children`, `height`, `index`, `isLeaf`, `.indices()` for no-crossing leaf order). API verified against the installed package's TypeScript source before use. Bundled into the component artifacts by esbuild (no external CDN), no postinstall scripts (no `allowBuilds` change needed).

## Clustering approach + complexity caveat

- Metrics: `euclidean`, `correlation` (1 − Pearson r; constant vectors → max dissimilarity). Linkage: `average`, `complete`, `ward`.
- Rows are clustered as vectors of length `ncols`; columns as vectors of length `nrows`. Leaves are reordered by the dendrogram's no-crossing leaf order so structure appears as blocks along the diagonal.
- **Complexity:** AGNES materializes a full n×n distance matrix and merges the two closest clusters each step — **O(n²) memory, ~O(n³) time**. Rows/cols are therefore auto-clustered **only when a dimension has ≤ 2000 leaves** (`MAX_CLUSTER_N`); above that the axis falls back to identity order. **The heatmap rendering itself scales far beyond that** (canvas). Larger inputs should pass a **precomputed** leaf order or dendrogram via `meta.rowLinkage` / `meta.colLinkage` to skip clustering; precomputed values are validated (length / permutation / index range) before use.

## Data contract

- `columns.values`: numeric buffer, **row-major**, length `nrows*ncols` (float32 via binary transport from Python; JSON array from R).
- `meta`: `{ nrows, ncols, rowLabels?, colLabels?, rowLinkage?, colLinkage? }`. A linkage may be a bare 0-based leaf-order array, or `{ order, merges: [{ left, right, height }] }` where leaves are `0..n-1` and internal node `k` is `n+k`.

## Options (camelCase, identical across JS / R / Python)

`metric` (`'euclidean'|'correlation'`), `linkage` (`'average'|'complete'|'ward'`), `colormap` (`'viridis'|'rdbu'` — from `@bioviz/core` ramps), `zScore` (bool, per-row standardize), `clusterRows`, `clusterCols`, `showRowDendrogram`, `showColDendrogram`, `showLabels`, `legendTitle`, `theme`. Diverging color domain is auto-symmetric for `rdbu` / z-score.

- **R:** `clustermap(mat, ...)` accepts a numeric matrix (dimnames → labels), row-major flatten, `clustermapOutput()` / `renderClustermap()` Shiny bindings.
- **Python:** `Clustermap(matrix, ...)` accepts a numpy 2D array or a pandas `DataFrame` (index/columns → labels), packs `values` as float32 row-major with shape/labels in `meta`.

## Files

Appends only the 3 shared files (`packages/components/src/lib/index.ts`, `packages/components/dev/main.ts`, `python/src/bioviz/__init__.py`), sorted. Everything else is new. Generated `man/*.Rd` + `NAMESPACE` committed. A dev demo mounts a synthetic block-structured, shuffled matrix so clustering visibly recovers the blocks.

## Verification (all pass from repo root)

- `pnpm install && pnpm dist` — builds + syncs `clustermap.js` (~90kb) into R & Python.
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" test` — 25 passed (18 clustermap pure-helper tests + volcano + core).
- `roxygen2::roxygenise("r/bioviz")` — clean; `devtools::test("r/bioviz")` — 31 passed.
- `pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest` — 11 passed (6 clustermap + 5 volcano).

Do not merge.

title: Hi-C contact matrix (WebGL)
description:
## Component

`hic` — a symmetric genomic **Hi-C chromatin contact matrix**. Large,
log-scaled intensity, smooth zoom/pan. Self-contained WebGL renderer — **no
HiGlass / tile server required**.

## Library + version

- **regl `^2.1.1`** (added via `pnpm --filter @bioviz/components add regl`;
  bundles its own TypeScript types, no `@types/regl` needed). No new
  `allowBuilds:` entries were required in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

## Rendering approach

The whole matrix is uploaded **once** as a single-channel (`luminance`) float
texture and drawn as **one textured quad**. The sequential colormap (viridis
LUT from `@bioviz/core`) and the log/linear transform run in the **fragment
shader**, so:

- Pan/zoom is just a UV-space affine transform on the quad — no re-upload, no
  per-cell DOM (`<rect>` per cell is never used).
- Recoloring on `vmax`/`transform` change is a uniform update.

SVG overlay carries only the low-cardinality layer: **genomic coordinate ticks**
(bp/kb/Mb when `binSize` is known, else bin index) on both axes and a **colorbar**.

### Level of detail

`buildLODPyramid` precomputes a mean-pooled pyramid (2×2 average, halving to a
64-bin floor) once per dataset. `pickLODLevel` chooses the coarsest level that
still shows ≥1 texel per device pixel **inside the visible window** (effective
resolution scales with the visible fraction), so a fully zoomed-out 1M-cell
matrix samples a small texture while a zoomed-in window uses full resolution.
Textures are lazily uploaded per level and freed on `destroy`.

## Data contract (dense + sparse)

Both converge on the shared `BiovizData`; `meta = { n, binSize?, chrom? }`.

- **dense**: numeric `values` (row-major, length `n*n`) via binary transport.
- **sparse**: columns `{ i: int32[], j: int32[], v: float32[] }`; filled into a
  dense buffer with `densifySymmetric` (mirrors across the diagonal when
  `symmetric`). Designed so multi-resolution/binned tiles could later feed the
  same renderer.

## Options (camelCase, identical across JS / R / Python)

`colormap` (`'viridis'`), `transform` (`'log'` | `'linear'`), `vmax`
(`null` = auto high percentile via an O(n) log-histogram), `vmin`,
`vmaxPercentile`, `symmetric` (default `true`), `label`, `theme`.

- **R**: `hic(mat, ...)` accepts a square matrix **or** an `i`/`j`/`v`
  list/data-frame; `hicOutput()` / `renderHic()` Shiny bindings.
- **Python**: `HiC(matrix, ...)` accepts a 2-D square numpy array **or** a
  COO-like triplet (tuple, mapping, or `i=`/`j=`/`v=` kwargs); numerics packed
  via `pack_columns`.

Publication export: `exportPNG` (rasterizes the canvas) and `exportSVG` (hybrid
figure — rasterized matrix cropped into an SVG `<image>` + vector axes/colorbar).

## Dev demo

`demos.hic` in `packages/components/dev/main.ts` renders a synthetic
**1024×1024 (~1M cell)** contact matrix with power-law distance decay, TAD-like
domains and off-diagonal loop dots.

## Verification (all pass from repo root)
